# The Mythos Imperative — Salesforce CRM Security Hardening

> A vendor-neutral, threat-informed hardening reference for the customer side of the Salesforce shared-responsibility partnership. Ten pillars from Identity to Defensive AI; nineteen appendices. Companion Salesforce DX reference implementation included.

Document version: 1.5.41
Last modified: 2026-05-18
Author: Dr. Paul Coleman
Canonical URL: https://drpaulcoleman.github.io/agentforce-mythos-hardening/
Repository: https://github.com/drpaulcoleman/agentforce-mythos-hardening
License: All rights reserved (c) 2026 Dr. Paul Coleman

## Overview

This is the customer-side defender's encyclopedia for Salesforce CRM security in the frontier-AI era. Most Salesforce breaches are not platform breaches — they are customer-side configuration, integration, and human-factor breaches (vishing, OAuth abuse, misconfigured Experience Cloud guest profiles, rogue browser extensions). The document provides structured hardening guidance across ten pillars, aligned to NIST CSF 2.0, OWASP Top 10, and CIS Critical Security Controls v8.

## Threat Landscape (2024–2026)

The document is threat-informed by these real-world campaigns:
- UNC6040: Vishing → malicious Connected App OAuth grant chain
- UNC6395: Salesloft/Drift ISV supply-chain compromise (700+ orgs)
- Krebs-pattern / DIVD-2026-00005: Experience Cloud guest user data exposure
- Browser-extension OAuth hijack (33 Chrome extensions, 2.6M users)
- AI prompt-injection via web forms
- Mythos supply-chain incident (April 2026): third-party vendor compromise, not direct Anthropic breach

## Ten Hardening Pillars

### Pillar 1: Identity & Authentication
- MFA factor matrix (what survives vishing)
- FIDO2/WebAuthn for Salesforce (passkeys, hardware keys, vault-stored)
- High Assurance sessions & step-up
- Custom Login Flows as a universal hook
- SAML/OIDC SSO architecture
- Custom Auth Providers + Apex handlers
- My Domain, Identity Verification, Device Activation
- Tier-based privilege gating (stock vs. bespoke)
- Authentication strength tiers (AMR/ACR signals)
- MFA enforcement roadmap (Jun–Jul 2026)
- Password vault roles post-passkey

### Pillar 2: Access Control & Least-Privilege Migration
- Organization-Wide Defaults (Private as foundation)
- Profile → Permission Set Group migration
- Role Hierarchy (visibility, not permission)
- Sharing Rules (ownership, criteria, guest red flag)
- Restriction Rules
- Field-Level Security and Apex run-mode contract
- Reports, List Views, Exports (exfiltration surface)
- Files/ContentDocument (silent leak path)
- Modify All Data / View All Data quarterly attestation

### Pillar 3: Experience Cloud Guest Hardening
- Persistent data-bleed mechanism anatomy
- "Secure Guest User Record Access" lineage 2021–2026
- Guest User Profile audit checklist
- Guest User Sharing Rules per-rule review
- LWC + Aura Controllers reachability problem
- Unauthenticated endpoint variants (DIVD-2026-00005)
- Public-Site surface (cache, URL, search-engine exposure)
- Automated scanner + public-site crawl pattern

### Pillar 4: Connected Apps & AppExchange Supply Chain
- Connected App → External Client App transition (Spring '26)
- OAuth flow ranking (recommended, blocked, removed)
- Block uninstalled Connected Apps + admin pre-approval
- Refresh-token TTL, rotation, revocation
- AppExchange Security Review (necessary, not sufficient)
- ISV repo compromise pattern (UNC6395 / Salesloft Drift)
- Vishing → malicious Connected App (UNC6040 kill chain)
- Browser extensions (invisible OAuth bypass)
- OAuth Usage Attestation + dual-agent metadata scan
- Salesforce-side IP reputation containment (enforced 2026-04-24)

### Pillar 5: API, mTLS & Certificate Rotation
- Named Credentials & External Credentials
- Mutual TLS (outbound and inbound)
- 2026 certificate transitions (DigiCert Global Root G2)
- Integration Users & per-user Named Principals
- API Client Allowlist + Pub/Sub API hardening
- Session ID handling — prohibited use cases, JWT-based ECA replacement, managed-package namespace-bypass risk

### Pillar 6: Secure Code, Components & Automation
- Apex run modes (USER_MODE as default)
- SOQL injection (bind variables, not concatenation; `Database.queryWithBinds()` as preferred dynamic pattern)
- LWC + Visualforce XSS, sanitization, manual DOM (Lightning Locker vs. LWS, CSP directive table, unsafe-tag table)
- CSRF defaults and the constructor-DML anti-pattern (incl. `renderedCallback`, "Require CSRF protection on GET requests" VF setting)
- Flow security (run context, guest-accessible problem, Apex-invoked-flow unconditional system mode, input validation)
- Shadow Flow / Outbound Messages (silent exfil vector)
- Email-to-Case / Web-to-Lead / Web-to-Case intake hardening
- Arbitrary redirect — `retURL` / `startURL` open-redirect hardening
- `postMessage`, clickjacking, and iframe embedding (`frame-ancestors`, origin validation, sandbox attribute)
- WebSocket security — origin validation and Cross-Site WebSocket Hijacking (CSWSH)

### Pillar 7: Data Classification, Encryption, Sandboxes & Backup
- Data classification (the prerequisite)
- Encryption layers (TDE, Shield Platform Encryption, BYOK)
- Field Audit Trail and retention
- Einstein Data Detect (continuous discovery)
- Sandbox security & Data Mask
- Backup, recovery, ransomware survival
- Hyperforce + External Key Management (EEE)
- Mask vs. Encrypt vs. Delete lifecycle
- GDPR, CCPA, EU AI Act compliance
- Outbound Email verified sender domain enforcement (Spring '26)

### Pillar 8: Detection, Response & Observability
- Health Check + Security Center
- Setup Audit Trail + Login History (free baseline)
- Real-Time Event Monitoring & retention reality
- Threat Detection (Shield / Event Monitoring)
- Enhanced Transaction Security (Block / MFA / Notify)
- Incident Response Plan + AI agent compromise scenario
- SIEM streaming
- Salesforce Mobile App MDM/MAM observability
- Extended Login Anomaly Detection + automated containment (Apr 2026)
- Time-Based Session Level Policy for Reports (2026-05-27)
- Anomalous Report Export step-up (ML-driven; 2026-07-13)

### Pillar 9: DevSecOps for DX & Org Lifecycle
- CI/CD secret management
- Static analysis as a gate
- Unlocked Packages + signed package enforcement
- Deployment approval workflow
- Metadata git-repo dual-agent scanning
- Sandbox refresh governance

### Pillar 10: AI Augmentation Across the Defense Stack
- Claude Security (Opus 4.7) — public beta May 2026
- OpenAI GPT-5.5 / GPT-5.5-Codex equivalent workflows
- Trust Layer pattern
- AI-assisted anomaly policy authoring
- AI as IRP companion (Claude Code on call)
- AI-assisted metadata audit + Health Check baseline
- Limits, guardrails, agent autonomy levels
- Tools comparison (Claude / ChatGPT / Cursor / Codex / Gemini / Copilot)

## Appendices (A–S)

- **Appendix A**: Incident-Response Runbook Templates (vishing, OAuth abuse, guest exposure, ISV compromise, browser extension hijack, AI agent silent compromise)
- **Appendix B**: Identity & Auth Code Reference (SAML JIT handler, registration handler, custom claims, login flow Apex)
- **Appendix C**: Apex Secure-Coding Reference (USER_MODE, Security.stripInaccessible, bind variables, guest controller patterns)
- **Appendix D**: Metadata XML Reference (ConnectedApp, External Client App, Named Credential, External Credential, Remote Site, CSP Trusted Site, SAMLSSOConfig, Auth Provider, Permission Set, PermissionSetGroup)
- **Appendix E**: Transaction Security Policy Reference (report event, bulk API event, login event, mass record)
- **Appendix F**: Profile → Permission Set Group Migration Playbook (discovery, decomposition, cutover, rollback, regression testing)
- **Appendix G**: Experience Cloud Audit + Dual-Agent Repo Scan (automated metadata scanner, public site crawl, cross-validator)
- **Appendix H**: Certificate Rotation Runbook (DigiCert Global Root G2, Feb 5/Mar 15, 200-day max, Named Credential, mutual TLS)
- **Appendix I**: Real-Time Event Monitoring Schema + Queries (event log objects, sample SOQL, login/report/API/bulk API events)
- **Appendix J**: SIEM Streaming Architecture (Splunk, Sentinel, Chronicle, Elastic, New Relic, Pub/Sub API, ETL/Lambda)
- **Appendix K**: AI Prompt Library (CISO governance, anomaly authoring, IRP companion, metadata audit, Health Check baseline)
- **Appendix L**: Cost & License Reference Table (Shield, Event Monitoring, Data Mask, Security Center, Privacy Center, SSPM vendors)
- **Appendix M**: Admin Hardening Checklist — First Actions (Day 1, Week 1, Month 1, Quarter 1 copy-paste actions)
- **Appendix N**: Standards & Framework Mapping (NIST CSF 2.0, CIS v8, ISO 27001, SOC 2, HIPAA, PCI DSS, GLBA, SOX, FERPA, EU AI Act)
- **Appendix O**: Breach-Notification Timing Matrix (GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA, state laws, SEC 8-K, NIS2, OAIC, PIPEDA, PCI DSS, GLBA, FERPA)
- **Appendix P**: Maturity Self-Assessment (interactive 0–5 scorecard per pillar)
- **Appendix Q**: Trailhead Alignment (Salesforce training modules, trails, superbadges, security badges)
- **Appendix R**: Salesforce Well-Architected Framework Mapping (Trusted, Secure, Compliant, Reliable, Adaptable, Resilient, Composable, Governed)
- **Appendix S**: Industry-Specific Overlays (Financial Services Cloud, Health Cloud, Public Sector, Industries/Vlocity, OmniStudio, B2B/B2C Commerce)

## Reference Implementation

A companion Salesforce DX project lives at `reference-impl/` in this repository. It contains:
- Working Apex classes with passing tests
- Deployable metadata configurations
- GitHub Actions CI pipelines
- Node.js tooling (scanners, crawlers)
- JSON data exports

See `reference-impl/README.md` for the doc-to-code map linking whitepaper sections to implementation artifacts.

- 2026-04-24: Salesforce IP reputation containment enforced

- 2026-06-10: Time-Based Session Level Policy enforced in production
- 2026-06-15: Dual-use certificate ban deadline (Salesforce compliance)
- 2026-06-22: MFA enforcement begins (privileged users)
- 2026-07-13: Anomalous Report Export step-up enforced in production

## How to Use This Document

1. **Executives / CISOs**: Start with the Executive BLUF and Talking-Point Cards
2. **Security architects**: Read the ten pillars sequentially; use the Risk Register and Critical Path Gantt for prioritization
3. **Admins with no budget**: Execute the 90-Minute Hardening Sprint immediately; follow Appendix M for Day-1/Week-1/Month-1 cadence
4. **Developers**: Focus on Pillar 6 (Secure Code) and Appendices B–E for code patterns
5. **Incident responders**: Use Appendix A runbook templates
6. **AI-assisted workflows**: Use Appendix K prompt library with Claude Security, ChatGPT, or equivalent tools
